notes: How this part was researched: the session's web-search allowance was already spent (the first search was refused), so every page was reached directly, with the kit's honest User-Agent and each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State, each county's, city's and school district's own site, party pages, Wikipedia's Minnesota election articles, and four news sites through their own search pages (KAXE, Lakeland PBS, the Chisago County Press and the Fairmont Sentinel). The reading tool was tried on six addresses; it read one of them (Erica Engelbert-Hensel's site). No search engine was read in place of the search tool. Most pages were read on the evening of October 1, 2026, and a few after midnight.

The filed websites were read from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) had been run; twelve of the thirty filed one, and each was then tried. Two more sites were found for candidates who filed none, Kim Wilson's and Jeff Reinert's: a handful of plausible addresses were checked for existence only (an address lookup, which sends nothing to any site), the few that existed were opened, and these two name the candidate and the race on their own pages. The others that existed were someone else's or empty and are not recorded.

Filed websites that could not be read or confirmed: dufaultformn.com answers with a CAPTCHA page (left alone; the website finding rests on the party page that links it); dulaneyforcitycouncil.com asks Claude by name to stay out in its robots.txt, so it was not read (the website finding rests on the City of Shakopee's own candidate list, which gives the address); reelectnovack.com has no address at all (a review item for Sean Novack). ericaformahtomedi.com answered the program's first try with 429 (too many requests); the reading tool read it, and so did a later try by the program. chipforsos.com is built by script: its title and description are in the page itself, and its About text (the own_words quote) was read from the site's own content file, https://chipforsos.com/api/content, which fills the About section of its home page.

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (403 to the reading tool; not asked again), so neither judge has a court page here; chisagogop.org (a CAPTCHA page); the Belle Plaine school district's site (the connection is refused or times out, for the program and the reading tool alike), so nothing could be checked for Genise Aretz; the site searches of Chisago County and CCX Media (robots.txt); stevenscountytimes.com (its robots.txt answered 403); and the newspapers whose robots.txt turns Claude away by name (the Forum Communications papers, hometownsource.com, presspubs.com, southernminn.com, twincities.com, minnlawyer.com, grandrapidsmn.com, willmarradio.com, myklgr.com).

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): three listings where a party unit publishes its backing in words that are not an endorsement. The Senate District 34 DFL lists Max Maher among its "Letter of Support Candidates", apart from its endorsed candidates; the Senate District 37 DFL lists him as a "DFL Supported Candidate", apart from its "DFL Endorsed" ones; the Senate District 35 Republicans list Sean Novack among nonpartisan candidates given "our support and recommendation", on a page whose title is "Endorsements". They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision. Two of those pages also describe the listed candidates' views in the unit's own words; that wording is not repeated here.

Read and left out on purpose: ages given as "age on Election Day" in KAXE's election guides (Melissa Maertens, Chip Tangen, Milo Scott), which do not fix a birth year; jobs, including Jennifer Vipond's (Grant County's Sheriff page calls her Chief Deputy) and Milo Scott's (KAXE: a Wadena police officer), and Chip Tangen's time as a congressman's legislative counsel; family details on the Anoka County page and on several campaign sites; labor and other non-party endorsements on Max Maher's site.

The two judges, Victoria Gardner and Sarah L. McBroom, are listed with no findings. Neither Lakeland PBS's nor KAXE's own search turned up an appointment story for McBroom, and no source that could be read covers Ramsey County's bench for Gardner. One KAXE local-news story, of April 20, 2026, calls McBroom an Itasca County judge (two more court stories came up in KAXE's search for her name and were not opened), but it is a story about another person's criminal case, so it is not offered as a source for her card and its address is not repeated here; KAXE's own search for her name finds it, if John or the second reader thinks otherwise.

Nothing was found for seven candidates, who are listed with no findings: Jennifer Vipond, Milo Scott, Jerome Niss, Eugenio Lopez, Genise Aretz, Victoria Gardner and Sarah L. McBroom. The Fairmont Sentinel (July 29, 2026) says of the six candidates for mayor that only Todd Smith has run for city office before; the Worthington district's School Board page does not list Eugenio Lopez among its members.

For the second reader: (1) Chris DuBose: no page read says in so many words that the 2026 candidate is the former commissioner; the tie is the name, the county, and the same contest twice (the Chisago County Press, November 4, 2022: the new District 2 pitted Rick Greene against Chris DuBose; the 2026 list has the same two names for District 2). The Press story of January 6, 2023 is at https://www.chisagocountypress.com/news/2023/jan/06/montzka-to-chair-citizens-boards-get-lots-of-new-f/ and the one of November 4, 2022 at https://www.chisagocountypress.com/news/2022/nov/04/voting-reminder/. His board service is given an end of 2022 because the December 16, 2022 story has him "working his final days"; the county's board page starts the next terms on January 3, 2023. (2) Danielle Plantz: the tie is the name and the city; New Hope's Human Rights Commission page lists a member of that name, and the list has the same name for New Hope City Council. (3) Barbara Neprud and Joshua Beulke appear on their districts' pages as Barb Neprud and Josh Beulke. (4) John P. Fahey's start year (2021) is from his own site; the county's page gives only the election year. (5) Kim Wilson's own_words quote is how she describes her candidacy on her About page, under the heading "WHY INDEPENDENT?"; the sentence goes on "because I believe my first responsibility should be to the people of District 47B, not to a political party". (6) Shaun C. Palmer's review item is only about the seat's name (District 5 in our record, Ward 5 to the city).

Seen in passing, for John: KAXE reports August 11 primaries for two nonpartisan county races in this part (Wadena County sheriff, five candidates; Crow Wing County Commissioner District 4), and Jeff Reinert's site gives the primary date too; our record carries no primary rows for nonpartisan offices. The Tri-City United School Board page spells another candidate on that list Hillary Birdsell (our list: Hilary Birdsell).

Second reader, October 2, 2026: every address in the candidates' findings was opened again with the kit's honest User-Agent, robots.txt obeyed. Two website findings were deleted (see "removed"); the notes above that describe them are the first reader's and are left as written. ericaformahtomedi.com answered the program with 429 four times and was read with the reading tool. chipforsos.com's own_words sentence is in the site's own content file (https://chipforsos.com/api/content), which fills its home page by script; Barb Neprud's "Elected: 2007" is in the page's own data on ci.k12.mn.us, which is also filled by script. reelectnovack.com still had no address. Mentions of KAXE's guides, of the Shakopee and Tri-City United Elections pages and of other pages whose addresses are not in this file were taken out of the findings' wording because they were not opened; the Chisago County Press stories of January 6, 2023 and November 4, 2022 named in the notes were opened and say what is quoted. Chris DuBose stays on the first reader's reasoning (same name, same county board, the same two names in District 2 in 2022 and 2026): John may want to look at it.
